Rob Hetland

Earth Scientist
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory

I study estuarine and coastal ocean circulation using analytical and numerical tools, focusing on better understanding and prediction of processes in the coastal ocean that control the transport and mixing of fresh water. I also apply these tools to coastal ocean ecology, particularly harmful algal blooms, eutrophication, and seasonal hypoxia.

Research focus

  • Regional Earth System Modeling
  • Estuaries & river plumes
  • Transport & mixing
  • Coastal ecology
  • Numerical modeling

Projects

All projects

GLEAM

Regional earth system modeling for subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction in the Great Lakes, linking the atmosphere, lakes, land, hydrology, and human systems.

SEAHORÇE

Coupling high-resolution regional ocean models with E3SM to better represent coastal processes and their interactions with the global ocean.

Integrated Coastal Modeling (ICoM)

Connecting coastal development, hydrology, and biogeochemistry through integrated models and rigorous comparisons.
